transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Skivone.
Dozens of homes near a Royal Air Force base used by U.S. bombers remain evacuated after
five men were arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist attack.
Maggie Blythe, temporary chief constable for Gloucestershire Constabulary, says the army's
explosive ordnance disposal unit continues to examine three vehicles near Wellford.
I would want to ensure and reassure our communities that any call into us is always acted on and
any information or intelligence passed to the police, again, is treated really seriously.
We will continue to do that.
We already do, and the same would apply to my colleagues from other agencies.
RAF Fairford hosts the U.S. Air Force's 501st Combat Support Wing and has been used by the
U.S. for strikes on Iranian missile sites in the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.
The White House has told Congress that it plans to "cancel" $810 million in health
care and educational-related programs.
As NPR's Mara Liasson reports, one prominent Republican is not happy about that.
In a statement on X, Senate Appropriations Committee Chair Susan Collins said the move,
known as a pocket rescission, is unlawful.
Collins, an incumbent Republican from Maine running for re-election, also said that the
rescissions were intended to "undermine Congress's constitutional power of the purse."
Regardless of how this separation of powers dispute is resolved, there are other cuts
to social safety net programs that were in the one big beautiful bill that are just now
kicking in, and they're hurting people who depend on Medicaid and food assistance.
That's another reason, along with higher prices at the pump or 7 percent mortgages, that voters
say they are angry and economically stressed—a bad sign for the incumbent party just weeks
away from the election.
Mara Liasson, NPR News.
Pope Leo told a massive crowd gathered at the Shrine of Lourdes that the Catholic Church
must confront deep wounds caused by clergy abuse.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports Leo is on a four-day visit to France.
Lourdes is a town in the foothills of the Pyrenees Mountains that attracts some 3 million
pilgrims a year for its purported healing spring waters on the spot where a 19th-century
shepherd girl had apparitions of Virgin Mary.
The site is also connected to a recent scandal.
The shrine's facade has a series of mosaics by a prominent religious artist accused of
abusing 20 women.
The story's tall mosaics have been covered for the pope's visit.
Leo has previously apologized for abuse scandals that have damaged the church's credibility.
On a trip to Spain in June, he told bishops they must listen to survivors and offer reparations.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
Drenching rains continued to saturate shorelines in the Northeastern U.S. today.
Another round of flooding hit low-lying areas of New York and New Jersey and led to power
outages in multiple Northeastern states.
This is NPR News in Washington.
The 2019 superhero epic "Avengers Endgame" is back atop box office charts this weekend,
and PR's Bob Mondello calls this encore addition a lucrative marketing gimmick.
Marvel will be opening Avengers doomsday in three months, and what better way to promote
it than to bring back Endgame?
Avengers!
Assemble.
With four minutes of unseen footage to stoke excitement for the new installment, fans showed
up hoping to catch a glimpse of Robert Downey Jr.
"He'll answer us to me."
Returning not as Iron Man, but as a supervillain.
"For I am Doom."
This weekend's $86 million in ticket sales puts Endgame, the second biggest earner in
Hollywood history, within striking distance of Avatar, currently the biggest, and it edged
the total box office hall for the 38-film Marvel Cinematic Universe above $35 billion.
Bob Mondello, NPR News.
In the race for baseball's National League wild card birth, the Philadelphia Phillies
beat the Tampa Bay Rays 7-3.
The Phillies now face a best-of-three wild card series against Atlanta.
Chinese pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang are now at Zoo Atlanta.
Having left Chengdu in southwestern China early today aboard a specialized FedEx Panda
Express, it's part of a new agreement between the U.S. and Chinese governments.
The loan of pandas is part of China's global diplomacy, the name of the male Ping Ping
means peaceful, the female's name Fu Shuang means double happiness.
I'm Louise Schiavone, NPR News, Washington.

topics.text: Five men arrested on suspicion of preparing terrorist attack near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire
White House plans to cancel $810 million in health care and educational programs
Republican Senator Susan Collins calls White House rescissions unlawful pocket rescissions
Pope Leo tells crowd at Lourdes shrine Catholic Church must confront clergy abuse wounds
Drenching rains cause flooding in New York and New Jersey with multiple power outages
Avengers Endgame returns to box office top with $86 million weekend earnings
Philadelphia Phillies beat Tampa Bay Rays 7-3 in National League wild card race
Chinese pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang arrive at Zoo Atlanta from Chengdu
